weather.tip: 90% rain chance tonight — carry an umbrella if you're heading out, and build in extra time on the road since Bengaluru's evening downpours reliably bring waterlogging and traffic snarls.

around.headline: BMTC conductor suspended after viral video shows him shoving a homeless man off a bus
around.summary: A conductor was suspended after video showed him pushing a homeless man off the footboard before he could board or explain himself, sparking wide outrage online. If you witness similar misconduct, a formal complaint (not just a viral post) is what actually gets action taken.
around.source: The Indian Express, Times of India

around.headline: SUV rollover near Bengaluru kills 2, injures 3
around.summary: An SUV toppled on the outskirts of the city, killing two people and injuring three others. Wear your seatbelt in every seat, including the back, and speak up if a driver is going too fast.

around.headline: Bengaluru policing to be split into five commissionerates
around.summary: The state government is pushing ahead with a plan to split Bengaluru into five police commissionerates, adding 6,633 posts and a Rs 765 crore outlay. If this goes through, expect your local station's jurisdiction and complaint routing to shift — watch for official notices in your area.
around.source: The Indian Express, The New Indian Express, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Karnataka HC orders BDA to restore 18-metre road plan, quashes 9.5m u-turn
around.summary: The High Court directed the Bangalore Development Authority to revert to an 18-metre road-width plan, striking down a prior 9.5-metre revision. If you live or commute near a BDA layout road, this could reopen width or acquisition questions in your area.

around.headline: RBI keeps repo rate unchanged at 5.25%
around.summary: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee held its policy rate steady this week. Your existing home or auto loan EMIs stay put for now — no immediate relief, but no hike either.

around.headline: Bengaluru Metro's airport line 72% complete, on track for phased 2027 opening
around.summary: BMRCL says construction on the airport metro line is 72% done and remains on schedule for a phased opening by 2027. Commuters planning around metro-to-airport connectivity shouldn't expect any timeline change for now.

events.note: The IAF's Training Command has confirmed Bengaluru will host Aero India again — worth marking your calendar early if you plan to attend.

events.name: BISFF 2026
events.note: India's only Oscar-accredited short film festival returns to Bengaluru — a solid pick if you're into cinema beyond the mainstream.

events.name: Lalbagh flower show — Western Ganga dynasty theme
events.note: This year's flower show at Lalbagh showcases the heritage of the Western Ganga dynasty — a low-key outing if you enjoy history with your greenery.

street_smart.title: A BMTC conductor turns aggressive and shoves a passenger off the bus before they can even explain themselves — and everyone else on board just watches.
street_smart.based_on: Today's viral video (multiple outlets) of a BMTC conductor shoving a homeless man off a bus before he could board or explain himself; the conductor has since been suspended. This is a fresh angle — bystander response and formal redressal for public-transport misconduct — not used in the last 3 weeks of briefs.
street_smart.situation: You're on a BMTC bus this evening when the conductor suddenly snaps at a passenger trying to board — shoving him off the footboard before he can pay or explain — much like today's viral video that got a conductor suspended. The bus rolls on, and no one else says or does anything. What do you do?

choices.text: Say nothing — it's not your business, and the conductor was probably provoked.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Assuming 'someone else will handle it' is exactly why this kind of misconduct keeps recurring unchecked on the same routes — today's conductor was suspended because riders came forward with video and a complaint, not because BMTC noticed on its own.

choices.text: Confront the conductor directly and demand an apology before you get off.
choices.feedback: Risky. Direct confrontation in a heated moment can escalate unpredictably, and you could end up as a second party in an assault complaint yourself. Documenting the incident is more useful than engaging in it.

choices.text: Film the incident and post it on social media, then move on.
choices.feedback: Risky. Video and public pressure help — it's part of how today's case surfaced — but a viral clip alone isn't a tracked complaint. Without a formal report, BMTC has no case file to act on, and footage can get buried in the news cycle within a day.

choices.text: Film the incident if it's safe to, note the bus number and route, and file a same-day complaint through BMTC's official complaint channel (app/website) or the Sakala grievance portal.
choices.feedback: Correct. A documented complaint with the bus number, route, time and evidence is what creates an actual case file BMTC has to respond to — that combination of public video plus a formal complaint is what got today's conductor suspended, not the video alone.

takeaways: Bystander silence is what lets recurring transit misconduct go unchecked — a documented complaint is what actually triggers action.
Always note the bus number and route before you get off; without it, even good video evidence is hard for BMTC to act on.
File through BMTC's official complaint app/website or Sakala the same day — social media pressure helps but doesn't substitute for a formal, trackable complaint.

quiz.question: What sparked today's BMTC conductor suspension?
options: A viral video showing him shove a passenger off before boarding
A dispute over a lost farecard
A passenger's inability to pay in cash
quiz.why: Viral-video-triggered suspensions like this one increasingly depend on riders also filing a formal complaint alongside the footage for the case to actually hold.

quiz.question: According to BMRCL, what percentage of Bengaluru Metro's airport line construction is complete?
quiz.why: The line is expected to open in phases rather than all at once, with the full stretch meeting a 2027 deadline.

quiz.question: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee this week kept the repo rate unchanged at what level?
quiz.why: A steady repo rate means existing floating-rate loan EMIs won't move immediately in either direction.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up roughly 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
quiz.why: Oxygen, the gas we associate most with breathing, makes up only about 21% of the air — nitrogen is the majority by far.

quiz.question: Under India's Constitution, 'Police' falls under which List, giving states primary control over policing?
options: There is no such list — it's unregulated
quiz.why: That's part of why states like Karnataka can restructure their own police commissionerates — such as today's proposed five-way split — without needing Parliament's approval.
